description: Read-only kernel and memory inspector. Lists every value under these keys; values documented here show their meaning and Windows default. Values can only be changed through the linked catalog item; values linked to a rejected entry are explained but never changed.

keys.name: Session Manager\kernel
keys.hint: Kernel object manager and timer settings.
keys.description: Settings read by the kernel at boot. Most values here are set by Windows itself; the timer-resolution value is the only one iG Windows Tuner catalogues.

values.name: GlobalTimerResolutionRequests
values.meaning: 1 restores the pre-2004 behaviour where one process's timer-resolution request affects the whole system.

values.name: ObCaseInsensitive
values.meaning: Object names are case-insensitive. 0 is only for POSIX subsystems and breaks normal Windows path handling.

values.name: DisableTsx
values.meaning: Intel TSX control used by speculative-execution mitigations. iG Windows Tuner never changes mitigation settings.

values.name: MitigationOptions
values.meaning: System-wide exploit protection settings written by Windows Security or Set-ProcessMitigation -System. Change them only through exploit protection.

values.name: MitigationAuditOptions
values.meaning: Audit-mode counterpart of MitigationOptions (exploit protection).

keys.name: Session Manager\Memory Management
keys.hint: Page file, pool and memory manager settings. Most popular tweaks here are obsolete or harmful.
keys.description: The memory manager sizes pools and caches dynamically on 64-bit Windows. The page file configuration is the only value iG Windows Tuner changes here (system-managed page file); the classic 'memory tweaks' are explained and rejected.

values.name: PagingFiles
values.meaning: Page file configuration. '?:\pagefile.sys' means a system-managed page file; 'C:\pagefile.sys 4096 8192' a fixed size; an empty list no page file.

values.name: ClearPageFileAtShutdown
values.meaning: 1 overwrites the page file at shutdown (security policy 'Shutdown: Clear virtual memory pagefile'); shutdowns get slower.

values.name: DisablePagingExecutive
values.meaning: 1 keeps kernel-mode code and drivers in RAM. No measurable benefit with enough memory.

values.name: LargeSystemCache
values.meaning: 1 favours the file cache over programs, a server setting that hurts desktop responsiveness.

values.name: FeatureSettingsOverride
values.meaning: Overrides speculative-execution mitigations. Set by tools that turn mitigations off.

values.name: FeatureSettingsOverrideMask
values.meaning: Mask that goes with FeatureSettingsOverride.

values.name: SecondLevelDataCache
values.meaning: Legacy L2 cache size hint from the Windows NT era. Modern Windows reads cache sizes from the CPU and ignores tuning here.

values.name: NonPagedPoolSize
values.meaning: 0 lets Windows size the non-paged pool dynamically (64-bit Windows does this well).

values.name: PagedPoolSize
values.meaning: 0 lets Windows size the paged pool dynamically.

values.name: SystemPages
values.meaning: 0 lets Windows size system page table entries dynamically.

values.name: SessionPoolSize
values.meaning: Session pool size in MB, a Windows default.

values.name: SessionViewSize
values.meaning: Session view space in MB, a Windows default.

keys.name: PriorityControl
keys.hint: Foreground boost and quantum settings. Popular 'priority separation' tweaks are placebo.
keys.description: Win32PrioritySeparation controls quantum length and the foreground boost. Windows' client default already favours the foreground window.

values.name: Win32PrioritySeparation
values.meaning: Quantum length and foreground boost. 2 is the client default (short, variable quanta with foreground boost).

values.name: IRQ8Priority
values.meaning: A Windows 9x-era myth; Windows NT ignores IRQ priority values here.

values.name: ConvertibleSlateMode
values.meaning: Tablet/laptop posture reported by convertible devices. Not a tuning value.

keys.name: Multimedia\SystemProfile (MMCSS)
keys.hint: Multimedia Class Scheduler settings that games and audio apps use to get CPU priority.
keys.description: MMCSS reserves CPU time for low-priority work while multimedia threads run and throttles non-multimedia network processing during playback. Values below 10 or above 100 are clamped to 20 by Windows.

values.name: SystemResponsiveness
values.meaning: Percentage of CPU guaranteed to low-priority work. Rounded down to tens; below 10 or above 100 is clamped to 20; 100 disables MMCSS.

values.name: NetworkThrottlingIndex
values.meaning: Limits non-multimedia network packet processing while MMCSS multimedia playback runs. 0xFFFFFFFF disables the throttling.

values.name: NoLazyMode
values.meaning: Undocumented community value. Not read by current Windows as far as Microsoft documents.

keys.name: MMCSS task: Games
keys.hint: Thread characteristics for games that register with MMCSS. GPU Priority and SFIO Priority are not used by Windows.
keys.description: Only applies to threads that call the MMCSS API for the Games task; most games do not. Microsoft documents GPU Priority and SFIO Priority as unused, so the popular edits have no effect.

values.name: Affinity
values.meaning: Processor affinity bitmask; 0 means no affinity.

values.name: Background Only
values.meaning: Whether the task has no user interface.

values.name: Clock Rate
values.meaning: Scheduling granularity hint (100 ns units); no guarantee since Windows 7.

values.name: GPU Priority
values.meaning: Documented by Microsoft as not used.

values.name: Priority
values.meaning: Task priority 1 (low) to 8 (high).

values.name: Scheduling Category
values.meaning: High, Medium or Low scheduling category.

values.name: SFIO Priority
values.meaning: Documented by Microsoft as not used.

keys.name: CrashControl
keys.hint: What Windows writes and shows when it stops with a blue screen.
keys.description: Startup and recovery settings: the dump type, where dumps go, and whether Windows restarts automatically. Changes take effect after a restart.

values.name: CrashDumpEnabled
values.meaning: 0 none, 1 complete, 2 kernel, 3 small (minidump), 7 automatic memory dump.

values.name: AutoReboot
values.meaning: 1 restarts automatically after a blue screen; 0 keeps the stop screen up.

values.name: DumpFile
values.meaning: Path of the kernel, complete or automatic memory dump.

values.name: MinidumpDir
values.meaning: Folder for small memory dumps.

values.name: Overwrite
values.meaning: 1 overwrites an existing memory dump file.

values.name: LogEvent
values.meaning: 1 writes an event to the System log after a stop error.

values.name: DisplayParameters
values.meaning: 1 shows the stop code parameters on the blue screen (community-known value, not documented by Microsoft).
